model_annotation: This plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of several methods as a function of co-occurrence number. The x-axis represents "Co-occurrence Number" on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 3 to beyond 3000, with tick marks at 10⁰ (implicitly), 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis represents "ACC (%)" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 38% to 65%, with tick marks at intervals of 5 percentage points. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different method. The black line with circle markers ("Base") starts at approximately 38% at a co-occurrence number of ~3, rises slightly to around 44% near co-occurrence number ~300, and then levels off at approximately 43.5% at the highest co-occurrence values. The light blue line with inverted triangle markers ("FT") begins at approximately 40% and increases gradually to about 47.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The red line with upward triangle markers ("IKE") starts at approximately 43% and rises steadily to about 49% at the rightmost point. The brown line with diamond markers ("MEND") begins at approximately 44.5%, increases to around 49% at co-occurrence ~30, continues rising to approximately 54% at ~300, and reaches about 56.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The purple line with pentagon markers ("MEMIT") starts at approximately 44% and increases to around 55% at the highest co-occurrence value, showing a relatively steady upward trend. The green line with square markers ("ROME") starts at approximately 51% at the lowest co-occurrence number, rises to about 57.5% at ~30, continues to approximately 62.5% at ~300, and reaches the highest value of approximately 66% at the largest co-occurrence number.
